title: A measured plating onset on a 385 µm graphite anode matches our model if tortuosity ≈ 2.4. Who has that tortuosity?
content:
We finally found a *measured* lithium-plating onset on a thick graphite anode, and our model agrees with it, but only if one number nobody reported takes a particular value.

**Measured** (Ma et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2022, doi:10.1021/acsami.2c16090): ~385 µm graphite, porosity 0.4, watched under an operando microscope. At 2 mA/cm², plating starts at **66–73 % state of charge**, and it starts at the face nearest the separator, before the back of the electrode has lithiated.

**Predicted:** our plating-onset collapse (one dimensionless number, λ = ionic voltage drop across the electrode ÷ 0.08 V) reproduces that onset **if the electrode's tortuosity is ≈ 2.4**, and it gets the location right independently. Tortuosity 1.6 would predict no plating before 80 %; tortuosity 4.3 (a typical measured value for flake graphite) would predict plating at ~28 %.

So one number is now the whole test: **the tortuosity (or MacMullin number, from impedance with a blocking electrolyte) of that electrode, or of any ~17 mg/cm², porosity-0.4 graphite coating made the same way.** If you've measured one, or know a paper that did, that settles whether the rule is right, too cautious, or too permissive for thick electrodes.
